In brief: A wet and warm week is expected in Abuja, with rainfall chances ranging from 56% to 78% each day, and temperatures fluctuating between 28°C and 30°C. The current conditions in Abuja are characterized by a relatively warm temperature of 24°C, which feels like 29°C due to the high humidity of 88%. The wind is blowing at a gentle speed of 6 km/h, and the UV index is at a moderate level of 3. As we look ahead to the week, models suggest that a low-pressure system will be dominating the weather pattern, bringing with it increased chances of rainfall. My best guess is that the heaviest rainfall will occur on Wednesday, with accumulation ranges expected to be between 20-40 mm.
### Monday The warm and humid conditions will persist, with temperatures expected to reach a high of 29°C and a low of 22°C. The rain chance is at 58%, with most of the rainfall occurring in the late afternoon to early evening hours. The wind direction will be from the southwest, blowing at a speed of around 10 km/h. In areas such as Maitama and Garki, the rain may cause some minor flooding, especially in low-lying areas. The humidity levels will be high throughout the day, making it feel quite muggy, especially in areas with dense vegetation such as the parks around Aso Rock. As the day progresses, the cloud cover will increase, reducing the amount of direct sunlight that reaches the ground. This will have a moderating effect on the temperature, keeping it from rising too high. However, the heat index will still be quite high, making it feel like it's around 32°C. In areas with poor drainage, such as some parts of Wuse, the rain may cause some flooding, especially during the peak hours of 4-6 pm. The good news is that the rain should clear up by the evening, leaving behind a relatively cool and pleasant night. The current traffic conditions on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway are light, with vehicles moving at a speed of 38 km/h, which is the same as the free-flow speed. This is likely due to the fact that it's still early in the week, and many people are still getting back into their routine after the weekend. As the day progresses, the traffic is likely to build up, especially during the peak hours.
### Tuesday The rain chance increases to 78% on Tuesday, with most of the rainfall occurring in the morning and early afternoon hours. The temperatures will be similar to Monday, with a high of 30°C and a low of 23°C. The wind direction will shift to the southeast, blowing at a speed of around 12 km/h. In areas such as Gwarinpa, the rain may cause some disruptions to outdoor activities, especially in the morning hours. The humidity levels will be even higher than on Monday, making it feel extremely muggy. As the low-pressure system strengthens, the cloud cover will increase, reducing the amount of direct sunlight that reaches the ground. This will have a moderating effect on the temperature, keeping it from rising too high. However, the heat index will still be quite high, making it feel like it's around 35°C. In areas with poor drainage, such as some parts of the airport road, the rain may cause some flooding, especially during the peak hours of 10 am-2 pm. The good news is that the rain should clear up by the evening, leaving behind a relatively cool and pleasant night. The traffic conditions on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway are likely to be heavy, especially during the peak hours, due to the increased rainfall and reduced visibility. The wind direction shift to the southeast may also cause some disruptions to the traffic flow, especially for vehicles traveling from the city center to the outskirts.
### Wednesday The rain chance remains high at 64% on Wednesday, with most of the rainfall occurring in the late morning to early afternoon hours. The temperatures will be similar to Tuesday, with a high of 30°C and a low of 22°C. The wind direction will shift to the northwest, blowing at a speed of around 10 km/h. In areas such as the National Assembly (NASS), the rain may cause some disruptions to outdoor activities, especially in the morning hours. The humidity levels will be slightly lower than on Tuesday, but still quite high. As the low-pressure system begins to weaken, the cloud cover will decrease, allowing more direct sunlight to reach the ground. This will have a warming effect on the temperature, causing it to rise to around 32°C. In areas with poor drainage, such as some parts of the city center, the rain may cause some flooding, especially during the peak hours of 11 am-3 pm. The good news is that the rain should clear up by the evening, leaving behind a relatively cool and pleasant night. The traffic conditions on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway are likely to be moderate, with vehicles moving at a speed of around 20-30 km/h. The current weather pattern suggests that the rainfall accumulation ranges will be around 20-40 mm, with some areas receiving more than others. My best guess is that the areas around Aso Rock will receive the most rainfall, due to the orographic effect of the hills.
